item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Monitoring and biological control of invasive insect species (CNR - Istituto per la Protezione Sostenibile delle Piante)
item.description:

Institution: CNR - Istituto per la Protezione Sostenibile delle Piante, Portici
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-03 Scienze e tecnologie dei sistemi arborei e forestali

The project aims to strengthen phytosanitary surveillance of invasive insect species by improving the capacity to detect and identify them promptly, study their spread and population dynamics, and assess the role of associated parasitoids. The results will support the work of regional technical staff and help inform monitoring and control strategies.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Biodiversity and nature-based solutions in urban contests (Univ. TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 13:00
Institution: Univ. TORINO, Turin
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-02 Agronomia e sistemi colturali erbacei e ortofloricoli

The research aims to analyze urban biodiversity and promote nature-based solutions for its conservation and enhancement within urban settings. Planned activities include surveying spontaneous and cultivated vegetation, analyzing and mapping species across various urban contexts, and testing solutions using native and ornamental species. Experimental work involves the propagation, cultivation, and monitoring of species—alternatives to invasive exotics—that are suitable for the various designed solutions. Data collection and statistical analysis will be conducted. Findings will be published in scientific journals, presented at conferences, and disseminated to the general public.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Effects of changing snow regimes on soil properties in alpine tundra (Univ. TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 13:00
Institution: Univ. TORINO, Turin
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

This research aims to investigate how changes in snow cover duration, depth, and distribution influence the physical and chemical properties and functioning of alpine tundra soils. Through multi-year monitoring and investigations along snow persistence gradients, the study will examine relationships among snow regime, soil temperature and moisture, vegetation, and organic matter and nutrient dynamics. The goal is to understand and predict changes in soil properties and functions in response to climate change.

This project aims to investigate the role of microbial interactions in fostering innovation within sustainable agri-food systems. The objective is to identify key microbial species and cooperative or competitive mechanisms that contribute to ecosystem stability, food quality, and the production of bioactive compounds. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Comparison of bolus and continuous nasogastric enteral feeding in critically ill dogs and cats (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/MVET-04 Clinica medica farmacologia e tossicologia veterinaria

This prospective randomised study will compare bolus and continuous nasogastric enteral feeding in critically ill dogs and cats. Eighty patients (40 per species) requiring tube feeding and an expected hospital stay of at least 48 hours will be enrolled with owner consent. Within each species, 20 patients will receive bolus feeds every six hours and 20 will receive continuous infusion over 20 hours daily. Caloric intake will increase progressively according to species. The primary objective is to assess nutritional efficacy and tolerability. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Microbiological valorization of digestate for the development of microbial inoculants for sustainable agriculture (Univ. PADOVA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-27 23:59
Institution: Univ. PADOVA, Legnaro (Pd)
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-08 Microbiologia agraria, alimentare e ambientale

MICRO-DIGEST aims to valorize digestate from agricultural biogas plants through the development of microbial inoculants for sustainable agriculture. The project includes characterization of the bacterial community of digestate, isolation and selection of plantgrowth-promoting bacteria (PGPB), assessment of relevant functional traits, and validation of the most promising strains on Zea maysL. under controlled conditions. Selected microorganisms will also be used to develop microbial inoculants using digestate as a low-cost growth substrate. The project integrates agricultural microbiology, plant physiology and microbial biotechnology within a circulareconomy approach.
